channel.title: Bloomberg — diagnostic source feed
channel.description: Diagnostic feed grouped by acquisition connector.

item.title: Broadcom Forecasts Boom in AI Chip Sales
item.description: Broadcom predicted a surge in artificial intelligence chip sales over the next two years, helping renew optimism that it can challenge Nvidia’s dominance in the lucrative market. The company also is on track to top earnings of $30 a share in fiscal 2028, outpacing Wall Street estimates. Bloomberg Intelligence analyst Matt Bloxham has the details. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Asia’s Economies Avert Energy Shock Via Fiscal Buffers, AI Boom
item.description: Asia’s economies from India to Malaysia and Australia defied all worst-case scenarios to post solid growth last quarter, as governments moved quickly to secure energy supplies and tapped relatively healthy balance sheets to cushion households.
item.dc:creator: Ruchi Bhatia and Srinidhi Ragavendran

item.title: Trump to Levy More Chip Tariffs to Boost Manufacturing
item.description: The Trump administration is weighing a fresh round of tariffs on imported semiconductors to lure more manufacturing to the US, Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick has said. Reporting from Semicon in Taiwan, Bloomberg's Stephen Engle says chip-supply-chain companies remain upbeat because AI chip demand is strong in the US. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Merck KGaA Electronics CEO on Business Strategy
item.description: Benjamin Hein, CEO of Electronics at Merck KGaA, discusses the company's business strategy and the outlook for the semiconductor industry. He speaks with Stephen Engle from the sidelines of Semicon Taiwan in Taipei. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: ByteDance Gets $30 Billion Loan, Asia’s Second-Largest This Year
item.description: ByteDance Ltd., the developer of TikTok, has secured a $29.6 billion loan, according to people familiar with the matter, in Asia’s second-largest dollar-denominated borrowing this year.
item.dc:creator: Janice Huang, Aileen Chuang and Kari Lindberg

item.title: Malaysia Set to Hold Rates as Investors Bet on Tightening Ahead
item.description: Malaysia’s central bank is expected to keep interest rates unchanged on Thursday, with subdued inflation giving policymakers little reason to tighten despite resilient economic growth.
item.dc:creator: Netty Ismail and Srinidhi Ragavendran

item.title: ZEISS SMT CEO: China 15 Years Behind in Top Chip Tools
item.description: Frank Rohmund, CEO of Zeiss SMT, a key supplier to ASML's EUV lithography machines, sayd he expects that Beijing will need 15 years to develop EUV lithography machine, and additional export controls will only accelerates innovation in China. He speaks with Bloomberg's Stephen Engle on the sidelines of Semicon Taiwan. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Chevron CEO Says Patience Pays Off in Venezuela Oil Deal
item.description: Big Oil has often employed the “hang around” playbook: secure legal rights to a giant resource — and then, eventually, figure out how to produce it profitably. But few companies have taken it to the extremes of Chevron Corp.
item.dc:creator: Kevin Crowley

item.title: Uber, Wayve Launch Robotaxi Service in London to Compete With Waymo
item.description: The centuries-old roads in the UK capital present challenges that Los Angeles and San Francisco don’t.
item.dc:creator: Olivia Solon and Natalie Lung

item.title: ASML Supplier Says China 15 Years Behind in Top Chipmaking Tools
item.description: China is about a decade and a half behind in developing cutting-edge chipmaking tools, according to a top executive at Germany’s Zeiss Group, a key supplier in the global semiconductor industry.
item.dc:creator: Christina Kyriasoglou and Stephen Engle

item.title: TikTok Backs Out of House Meeting to Avoid Kids Safety Questions
item.description: TikTok dropped out of an upcoming meeting with the House Select Committee on China on national security issues, saying it couldn’t participate because of unrelated child-safety litigation, the leader of the panel said.
item.dc:creator: Alexandra S. Levine

item.title: Markets Rebound as Oil, Yields & AI Remain in Focus | The Close 9/2/2026
item.description: Bloomberg Television brings you the latest news and analysis leading up to the final minutes and seconds before and after the closing bell on Wall Street. Today's guests are Alger Executive Vice President, Portfolio Manager Ankur Crawford, ProShares Head of Research, Active Investments CIO Alessio De Longis, Oppenheimer Managing Director & Senior Analyst Brian Nagel, MongoDB CEO CJ Desai, Edward Jones Head of Investment Strategy Mona Mahajan, DigitalBridge CEO Marc Ganzi, Skylar Capital Management Managing Partner & CIO Bill Perkins, Magnetar Capital Founder Alec Litowitz, & NBA Hall of Famer Shaquille O’Neal. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: CJ Desai Says MongoDB’s AI Momentum Is Real, But Guidance Remains Prudent
item.description: CJ Desai, CEO of MongoDB, says MongoDB feels very good about demand, noting Atlas delivered its fifth straight quarter of 29% growth and that total Atlas dollars continue to rise quarter over quarter. He speaks with Romaine Bostick & Sally Bakewell on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: DigitalBridge's Ganzi Says Data Centers Are 'Not the Villain'
item.description: Marc Ganzi, CEO of DigitalBridge, says AI infrastructure investing needs a diversified approach, but argues the real bottleneck is power. Speaking with Romaine Bostick on "Bloomberg The Close," Ganzi also says the industry cannot focus only on chips or software and stresses that the AI buildout should not be politicized. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: US Strikes Light-Touch AI Regulation Accord With G20 Members
item.description: Representatives from the world’s largest economies unanimously agreed to adopt guidelines proposed by the US that call for a lighter touch toward governing artificial intelligence and other emerging technologies, handing a win to the Trump administration and Silicon Valley.
item.dc:creator: Maggie Eastland

item.title: Microsoft to Disclose Azure Sales After Investor Gripes
item.description: Microsoft Corp. will begin disclosing quarterly sales for its Azure cloud unit, reversing course after years of criticism from Wall Street regarding a lack of information about the company’s most important growth engine.
item.dc:creator: Brody Ford and Matt Day

item.title: Broadcom Predicts Surge in AI Chip Sales Over Next Two Years
item.description: Broadcom Inc. predicted a boom in artificial intelligence chip sales over the next two years, helping renew optimism that it can challenge Nvidia Corp.’s dominance in the lucrative market.
item.dc:creator: Dina Bass

item.title: HPE Slides After Sales Boost Falls Short of Highest Expectations
item.description: Hewlett Packard Enterprise Co. declined in late trading after the company reported increasing sales that didn’t meet high expectations from investors, who have seen the stock price more than double so far this year.
item.dc:creator: Dina Bass

item.title: Thoma Bravo’s Proofpoint Is Said in Talks to Acquire Varonis
item.description: Thoma Bravo-backed Proofpoint Inc. is in talks to acquire cybersecurity company Varonis Systems Inc., which would be one of the biggest technology take-privates since the steep selloff in software stocks earlier this year, according to people familiar with the matter.
item.dc:creator: Ryan Gould

item.title: Tencent-Backed Enflame’s IPO Draws 4,073 Times Retail Demand
item.description: The initial public offering of Shanghai Enflame Technology Co., a company backed by Tencent Holdings Ltd., drew heavy demand from retail investors, as the last of the so-called “four little dragons” of leading Chinese artificial intelligence chipmakers taps the public market.
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg News
